manifest.prompt: make a compact, minimal, modern shopping component.
consumers: review the component against the brief
manifest.built: one agent, no helpers: 6 web searches (snippets read, not fetched), 7 pages read as text (WCAG 2.2, Laws of UX x2, Baymard, MDN x2), no screenshots, no references, no moodboard
how_to_read: 1. Read the head first: the first 33 lines hold manifest, essence and routing (Read limit=33, or jq '{manifest, essence, routing}' minimal-shop-component.metadump.json).
2. Pick the route for your job and run its jq: jq '<routing[i].jq>' minimal-shop-component.metadump.json
3. Also pull the anti-keywords and review prompts (checks) for your scope: jq '.anti_keywords, .checks' minimal-shop-component.metadump.json
4. Look up any term (lowercase): jq '.index["<term>"]' minimal-shop-component.metadump.json  -> hits give id + path; not_meant lists senses to avoid.
5. Grep works too: every entry is one line, so grep -n '<word>' minimal-shop-component.metadump.json returns whole entries.

poles: minimal: few visible parts and quiet surfaces
unmistakable: the add action is labeled and easy to hit

task.is: a compact, minimal, modern shopping component (a product card that lets a shopper add an item)
ladder: UX and UI design principles: choice, target size, feedback
accessibility standards: WCAG 2.2, live regions, reduced motion
e-commerce product cards and add-to-cart patterns
this compact, minimal, modern shopping component
its sizes, colors, states and timing
job: find the product in a list
see a confirmation of what was added
review the bag or check out

readings.reading: one product card with quick add and a compact confirmation of what was added
a product buy box with variant, quantity and add
a compact bag line with quantity stepper and subtotal
a product list of compact cards with a filter row

brief._about: The user's own words (prompt verbatim: 'make a compact, minimal, modern shopping component.'). Anchors are verbatim spans of the prompt.

b-compact.text: Compact: a small footprint with few parts; spacing is tight but never cramped, and the whole job fits in one small card or panel.

b-minimal.text: Minimal: every visible element earns its place. Keep what is needed to act and to read the product; remove the rest.

b-modern.text: Modern: contemporary restraint (neutral surfaces, clean sans-serif type, one accent, precise small radii), not futurism, glow or decorative effects.

b-component.text: A reusable UI unit that shows one product and lets a shopper act on it, not a whole storefront page.

ux_principles._about: Laws and heuristics a senior UX practitioner brings to a compact purchase control. Load-bearing parts were checked against fetched sources.

ux-hick.text: Decision time grows with the number and complexity of choices, so the compact component shows one primary action and few secondary ones.
never_implies: hiding options a shopper needs to decide

ux-fitts.text: Time to hit a target depends on its distance and size, so the add control is large enough to hit and sits beside the price, where the eye lands after reading the product.

ux-feedback-confirmation.text: After an add, confirm the specific item and quantity just added so the shopper can check it; a bare 'added' with no item detail weakens trust.

ux-recognition.text: Show the item name and current quantity on the card itself, so the shopper does not have to remember what they tapped.

accessibility._about: WCAG 2.2 and MDN requirements a component of this kind meets. Quotes are short; figures are the standard's own.

ac-target-size.text: Pointer targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS px (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8, Level AA), or spaced so undersized targets do not overlap another target.

ac-contrast.text: Normal text has contrast of at least 4.5:1 against its background (SC 1.4.3, Level AA); large text (18 pt, or 14 pt bold) needs 3:1.

ac-reduced-motion.text: The reduced-motion setting asks the interface to remove, reduce or replace motion; a short opacity or color change can stand in for a slide or scale.

ac-live-region.text: Announce the add confirmation in a polite live region, so screen readers hear it without interrupting the task in progress.

ac-labels.text: Each control that is icon-only, such as a minus or plus, gets a text accessible name like 'Decrease quantity' and 'Increase quantity'.

ecommerce_patterns._about: Patterns from e-commerce guides (search-result summaries, not fetched pages), so they are inferred and tier 2 at most.

cp-card-anatomy.text: Common card contents: image, product name, price, optional rating, one line of variant or spec, and one add control.

cp-add-visible.text: Guides warn that add-to-cart is often visually buried; keep it visible at rest on every screen size, with contrast and spacing that keep it the strongest action on the card.

cp-add-labeled.text: The add control carries a text label, not an icon alone.

cp-stepper.text: Minus and plus buttons with text labels; the limit state is shown both visually and to assistive tech; the quantity updates on each press without shifting the layout.

cp-variant-line.text: When the product has one variant, a single line such as '250 ml' replaces a selector.

anatomy._about: How the default reading is laid out. Builder's layout choice: the alternatives live in decisions.

an-stack.text: Image on top at a fixed aspect ratio; then name and price on one row; then the variant line; then the add row with stepper and add button.

an-price-first.text: The price sits on the same row or directly above the add row, so the decision happens in one place.

an-layers.layer: product data, presentation, interaction, bag state
an-layers.text: Product data (name, price) comes from data; presentation (layout) and interaction (add state) are the component's; the bag count belongs to the bag, not the card.

states._about: Interaction states the component needs. Inferred from patterns; each is a state to design, not a fixed look.

st-rest.text: Image, name, price, add control; no hover-only content.

st-focus.text: A visible focus ring on the add control and stepper buttons, separate from the hover look.

st-pending.text: The add control shows a brief in-progress label while the add request runs; the control stays the same size.

st-added.text: The control confirms with text such as 'Added: 2 in bag' for a short time, then returns to rest; the same text is announced politely.

st-limit.text: At the minimum or maximum quantity the matching stepper button is disabled and a short text note says why.

copy._about: Example labels. Illustrative good and bad lines written from the model's own copy knowledge.

cy-add.text: Short verb-first labels that name the destination.

cy-confirm.text: The confirmation names the item and quantity in plain words.

look_and_feel._about: Brand-agnostic look for modern minimal retail, distilled from the brief and general practice. Values are tokens to set, not measured specs.

lf-palette.text: Neutral surfaces and two text tones; one accent color reserved for the primary add control, so the eye goes there first.

lf-type.text: Clean sans-serif in two or three sizes: name, price (the strongest number), small meta; no decorative faces.

lf-space.text: Spacing follows one small scale; generous air around the image and between groups, so dividers are rarely needed.

lf-surface.text: Flat surface with a hairline border or none and a small corner radius; at most one soft shadow, shown on hover or focus.

lf-image.text: The product image sits on a neutral field at one fixed aspect ratio so cards align in a grid.

motion._about: Motion options, not requirements: illustrative timing for the add feedback and its reduced-motion fallback.

mo-add-feedback.text: Add feedback runs about 150 to 200 ms with an ease-out curve; no bounce, no travel across the card.

mo-reduced-fallback.text: Under the reduced-motion setting, the added state changes color or text at once, with no movement.

decisions._about: Options, not requirements: decision points the brief leaves open, each with the tradeoff and when each option fits.

dec-quick-add.decision: Add from the card, or open the product page first?

options.fits_when: the product has one variant or the variant is already resolved
size, color or fit must be chosen first

dec-quick-add.text: Quick add keeps the path short; the detail page keeps choices visible.

dec-stepper-place.decision: Stepper inline on the card, or in a small drawer?

options.option: inline stepper beside the add button

options.fits_when: quantity ranges are wide or the card is very small

dec-stepper-place.text: Inline is the compact default; the drawer trades speed for room.

dec-confirm-form.decision: Inline text on the control, a bag count change, or a small toast?

options.option: inline text on the add control
options.fits_when: the card is the whole context
a site header with a bag count is present
the add happens from a long list and feedback must reach the top of the screen

dec-confirm-form.text: Inline keeps focus where the shopper is; the badge and toast suit wider pages.

dec-sticky-mobile.decision: Pin the add control to the bottom on long mobile pages?

options.fits_when: the card is taller than the screen
the card fits in one screen

dec-sticky-mobile.text: Search summaries report sticky add bars help on long mobile product pages; treat that as unverified.

dec-touch-44.decision: Use 44 px touch targets instead of 24 px?

options.fits_when: the WCAG minimum is the floor and the layout is tight

dec-touch-44.text: A single blog recommends 44 by 44 px; this is not checked against a standard, so it stays an option.

dec-variant-select.decision: Single variant line, or a selector?

options.fits_when: two or three variants shown inline

dec-variant-select.text: The default reading assumes one variant.

associations._about: What the model associates with minimal modern retail. Seed material, not facts.

as-descriptors.text: Calm, quiet, considered, airy, precise, unhurried, honest; people say 'nothing extra'.

as-brands.text: Restrained product retail often cited: Muji, Aesop, Apple Store product pages. Take the descriptors and the spacing discipline, not the visuals.

as-metaphors.term: one object on a plain table
as-metaphors.text: A single product on a plain surface, lit evenly, with nothing competing.

parameters._about: Illustrative values, options not requirements. Starting points to adapt, not measured specs.

p-card-width.text: Card width in a grid of two to four columns.

p-radius.text: Small radius for card and controls.

p-type-name.text: Name about 15 px, price about 17 px, meta about 13 px.

s-mdn-reduced-motion.title: MDN: prefers-reduced-motion
s-mdn-reduced-motion.quote: The setting is used to convey to the browser on the device that the user prefers an interface that removes, reduces, or replaces motion-based animations.

s-mdn-aria-live.title: MDN: aria-live
s-mdn-aria-live.quote: When set to polite, assistive technologies will notify users of updates but generally do not interrupt the current task.

s-lawsofux-hick.title: Laws of UX: Hick's Law
s-lawsofux-hick.quote: The time it takes to make a decision increases with the number and complexity of choices.

s-lawsofux-fitts.title: Laws of UX: Fitts's Law
s-lawsofux-fitts.quote: The time to acquire a target is a function of the distance to and size of the target.

s-baymard-atc.title: Baymard: added-to-cart confirmation examples
s-baymard-atc.quote: lack adequate details about the just-added item risk users losing confidence in the site
